subject: Dedicated capacity: throughput / commit clarifications
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@hudsonbio.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hudsonbio.com, priya.raj@hudsonbio.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal — throughput & commit questions

Hi Aisha / Ben,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the slide deck internally and have a few follow-ups before we share with procurement:

- Can you confirm the recommended GPU pool size for our expected steady-state workload (outlined below)?
  - Peak QPS: ~220 requests/minute for embeddings + 45 requests/minute for chat generation (peak bursts up to 700 QPS for short windows)
  - Average context length: 1.2k tokens (most chat calls ~512 tokens; occasional 4k)
  - Concurrency target: 180 concurrent user sessions during peak
- What throughput SLA (p50/p95) can Redwood commit to for the Dedicated pool?
- Pricing: our procurement team is looking for committed-month pricing for a 12-month reserved pool + tiered discounts if we commit more capacity in year two.

We have a target internal spend band — procurement will push for a blended discount as we step up commits. Attaching the high-level workload doc.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
Hudson Biotech

Attachments: hudson_workload_summary.xlsx (referenced)

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@hudsonbio.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — throughput & commit questions

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifications so we size the pool correctly:

- When you say 220 reqs/min for embeddings, is that concurrent embedding generation (i.e., many small calls) or batched/async jobs?
- For chat generation: are the 45 reqs/min long-running sessions (multi-turn) or one-off prompts? If multi-turn, how many turns on average?
- For the 700 QPS burst: how long do bursts last (minutes / hours)? Are they predictable (scheduled runs) or ad hoc?

Preliminary ask from our side: please share a 24h sample CSV (timestamped QPS and average tokens per call) so we can run our throughput model. If procurement wants a pricing anchor now, we can share a recommended pool and a 12-month commit offer subject to the sample.

I'll pull Ben and Marissa in for sizing + commercial.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0127

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@hudsonbio.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — throughput & commit questions

Tom / Team — ran a quick back-of-envelope based on the numbers you shared and some conservative assumptions. Notes and a recommended starting configuration below. If you send the 24h sample we can refine.

Assumptions we used
- Embeddings: avg 500 tokens per request, efficient batching expected (20–40 requests per batch during steady-state)
- Chat gen: avg 1.2k tokens per response, KV cache used for multi-turn sessions
- Bursts: assume 10–30 minute windows at 700 QPS, infrequent (~2-3/month)

Sizing recommendation (starter pool)
- 6 x H100- or equivalent GPU instances (shared into a dedicated pool) configured with continuous batching and prefix caching.
- Expected steady throughput: ~25K tokens/sec aggregate; p50 latency for single-turn chat ~120–180ms, p95 ~420–800ms depending on context length and burst behavior.
- Concurrency: supports ~200 active sessions (matches target) with configured request queueing and burst buffer.

Pricing / commit anchor (12-month reserved pool) — initial proposal- Base monthly commit: $120,000 / month (reserved pool with 6 GPUs, 99.9% control-plane SLA)
- Included: 5 TB token cache snapshot retention; 24/7 infra support; quarterly workload reviews
- Discounting framework: 12-month commit = baseline price; 24-month commit = 10% off; ramp to 36-month or volumetric commit can unlock up to 18% off listed price (subject to throughput and consumption floors).

Optional add-ons (examples)
- Burst credit package (covers 3 large bursts/month): +$8K/month
- Dedicated networking (VPC peering + private link): +$3.5K/month

Next steps
- If you can share the 24h sample CSV (timestamps, tokens per call), we will run the model and return a refined config and a formal quote (including SKU-level pricing and a draft SOW).

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Architect, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Attachment: hudson_draft_commit_terms.pdf (pricing anchor, draft terms)

From: procurement@hudsonbio.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: priya.raj@hudsonbio.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — throughput & commit questions

Hi Aisha / Ben,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the sizing note. Procurement reviewed the anchor and has initial feedback:

- We are looking for a guaranteed throughput SLA (p95) for chat generation at the 12-month commit level; target p95 <= 700ms. Can Redwood accept SLA credits tied to that metric?
- Pricing: Hudson can agree to a 12-month committed pool but will need a 20% discount on the baseline if we do not take a 24+ month commitment. Alternatively, for a 12-month deal we can do a tiered usage ramp (50% month 1 minimum, 100% by month 4) if Redwood can provide a stepped discount schedule.
- Security/compliance ask: please provide SOC 2 Type II report and details on KMS/HSM key control for private deployments.

We are prepared to move quickly if we can align on: 1) an SLA construct with credits, 2) a clearer discount cadence for a 12-month commit, and 3) access to security artifacts.

Regards,
Priya Raj
Procurement Manager | Hudson Biotech

[Hudson Bio] Please include the procurement team on the formal quote and SOW.

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: procurement@hudsonbio.com, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@hudsonbio.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — throughput & commit questions

Priya / Team — thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses and a proposed path forward: 

SLA & credits
- We can include a p95 latency SLA for chat generation at the 12-month commit level: target p95 <= 700ms with service credits (2% monthly credit per missed SLA, capped at 20% per month). We will add clear measurement windows and an agreed sampling method in the SOW.

Pricing / discount cadence for 12-month commit
- We cannot extend a straight 20% off the baseline for a single-year deal given the upfront capacity reservation, but we can offer an 18% discount if Hudson: 1) signs a 12-month reserved pool at the recommended starter size (6 GPUs) and 2) agrees to the month-to-month ramp schedule (50% min M1, 75% M2, 100% M4).
- If you require the 20% discount, we can do that for a 24-month commit or for a 12-month commit plus a $72k upfront prepay (applied to months 1–6).

Security artifacts
- Attaching SOC 2 Type II summary and a KMS overview; Sean will send the detailed link to our compliance portal.

Next steps
1) Hudson provides the 24h request + tokens CSV (as requested by Ben).
2) Redwood will produce a final SKU-level quote, a revised SOW (sow_hudson_v1.docx) and the DocuSign envelope for the 12-month, 18% discount path.
3) If procurement prefers the 20% route, indicate preference for 24-month commit or confirm prepay.

I'll loop in our legal/commercial reviewer once you confirm the path. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: sow_hudson_v1.docx, SOC2_summary.pdf
